title: Batch-generated 58 looping sprite sheet animations with MiniMax H3 on 8GB VRAM — the first=last frame trick and what broke
author: RsetX
selftext:
Spent a night running MiniMax H3 through ComfyUI to make a game asset pack —

10 animals, 58 looping animations. Sharing what actually mattered, since most

of it was non-obvious.

**Loops close by construction, not by prompting.** H3 takes \`first\_frame\` and

\`last\_frame\`. Wire the same LoadImage into both and the animation is forced

back to its starting pose. I wasted several generations asking the prompt

nicely before realising the node already solves it.

**Length is 17k+5, not arbitrary.** 5, 22, 39, 56... 56 frames at 24fps =

2.33s. There's no fps parameter — the model was trained at 24, so fewer frames

means less \*motion\*, not slower playback.

**Scale the subject down before generating.** My source illustrations filled

90%+ of the canvas with 2% margin. The moment an animal extended a leg it

clipped. Cropping the subject, shrinking to 80% and recentering on white

fixed every clipped frame.

**Timing on a 3050 8GB, lowvram, --cache-none:** \~5min sampling, \~3.5min VAE

decode, 8.7min total per 56-frame 448×448 clip. WAN 2.2 5B failed here — VAE

decode thrashed at 7.93/8GB and never finished after 45 minutes. H3's VAE is

smaller and fits.

**Polling ComfyUI's API needs to tolerate timeouts.** During VAE decode the

HTTP server stops responding for tens of seconds. My first batch script only

caught HTTPError, so a TimeoutError killed a generation ten minutes in. Catch

URLError/TimeoutError/OSError and retry — a timeout means "busy", not "failed".



Pack's on itch [https://shaddafare.itch.io/shepherds-farm-animated-sprites](https://shaddafare.itch.io/shepherds-farm-animated-sprites) if anyone wants the output, but the above is the useful part.
